response: Prostatic syndrome and pleural effusion can be related but are not the same disease. Although they can occur independently, in some cases, they may be associated with each other, particularly if there is a neoplasm present. For instance, prostate cancer can metastasize to the lungs, leading to pleural effusion. It is essential to determine if the lesion is a metastasis, as the prognosis depends on the second tumor. Therefore, it is crucial to consider the possibility of synchronous tumors in patients with urinary and pulmonary symptoms suggestive of a neoplasm.
